title: Independent magnitude draws gave larger-first pair order in a six-cell deep-earthquake branching test
abstract: We tested whether larger-first earthquake pair order requires dependent magnitude draws. We used 785 deep ComCat events in 2000-2025 to set a magnitude slope, event count and background locations. We ran 400 catalogs in each of six branching-model cells. Each new magnitude was drawn independently. With magnitude-dependent productivity, a global label-shuffle test rejected in 99.0% to 99.75% of catalogs. With constant productivity it rejected in 4.0% to 5.25%. An exact expectation for direct parent-child edges explains the sign. This is a test of a method, not a fitted physical explanation of the source catalog. One source snapshot, a simplified delay law, selected model parameters and no detection model limit use.

display.caption: Left: shuffle rejection fractions with 95% Wilson intervals from 400 simulated catalogs per cell. Right: mean signed pair scores with central 95% simulation ranges. All new magnitude draws are independent. Alpha controls dependence of offspring count on parent magnitude. The dashed score is the observed deep-catalog value.

citations.reason: The regional shuffle result and its stated causal limit set this simulation question. Source data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
